items.cheapest_check: From a network outside the firm, request a zone transfer from each nameserver (dig AXFR wrenfield.example at each one); a refusal settles it.
items.unknown: Whether either nameserver answers a zone transfer request from an outside address (C2).
items.why: An open transfer hands anyone the zone's full record list, including names not otherwise published; DNS-NS-02 stays Unknown until it is tested.

items.cheapest_check: The mail platform's documentation on DANE, or a TLSA query for its published mail server names.
items.unknown: Whether the hosted mail platform supports DANE for inbound mail (E2).
items.why: DNS-TLS-04 applies only where the platform supports DANE; until that is known it stays Unknown.

items.cheapest_check: Sign in to the second account and read every domain's state, including expired and redemption, and its recovery contacts.
items.unknown: The full contents of the second registrar account (A4).
items.why: Domains in nobody's inventory expire or get hijacked unnoticed; DNS-REG-05 cannot be settled from the active list alone.

items.cheapest_check: Read the last month of DMARC aggregate reports for the marketing platform's sending sources.
items.unknown: Whether the marketing platform still sends anything using the domain (D3).
items.why: If it still sends, removing its SPF include (F-2) breaks that mail; if it does not, the include only authorizes a service nobody controls.

items.cheapest_check: Look up who holds the nameservers' domain and addresses, and ask the former vendor whether it still runs them.
items.unknown: Who operates the delegated nameservers for projects.wrenfield.example today (F4).
items.why: If the former vendor no longer runs them, whoever does controls a subdomain of the firm's domain, the same exposure as Chain B by another route.
